chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from 'Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about one who goes out from his family with falcons, hawks, and dogs, taking recreation for one night, two nights, or three: does he shorten his salat (prayer), or does he not shorten? So he عليه السلام said: He has only gone out in amusement, so he does not shorten.

key_terms.يَتَنَزَّهُ: he goes out for recreation or leisure
key_terms.يَقْصُرُ: he shortens the prayer during travel

ai.seo_question: Does a person traveling for recreational hunting shorten salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a person who travels for recreational hunting or amusement with hunting birds and dogs. The Imam عليه السلام states that such a journey is one of diversion, so the traveler does not perform qasr and must offer the prayer in full.
